tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.

tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

1	# spec-domain2.md — Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub (Domain 2)
2	> this spec was built from updated, PA2 requirements
3	
4	## AI Usage Log
5	
6	| Item | Detail |
7	|---|---|
8	| Conceptual AI contribution | ~35% AI / ~65% me |
9	| My part | Copied the standardized Domain 2 text (section 5) unchanged; walked through each requirement and endpoint and made every interpretation decision in section 6; directed which PA1 spec sections to carry over (overview, tech stack, deployment, layout, roles, out of scope) and how to adapt them |
10	| AI part (Claude chat assistant) | Listed open questions and options for each requirement and endpoint; drafted the wording of section 6 and the mock data from my decisions; adapted the carried-over PA1 sections to the standardized spec |
11	| Design-aid prompts | `PA2/.ai_logs/2026-11-14_spec-walkthrough-log.md` |
12	
13	## 1. Overview
14	
15	The Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub is one backend service of the Project Portal (PP). It manages a pool of physical lab equipment, software license keys and cloud credit vouchers, and handles requests for them from courses and research labs through a help desk ticket flow: request, sign-off, allocation, and for physical devices, return.
16	
17	The hub runs in its own containers, owns its own database and makes no calls to other Project Portal services. Data owned elsewhere (courses, labs, projects, users) comes from static mock data (section 7).
18	
19	Section 5 is the standardized specification for this service, copied unchanged. Section 6 clarifies the parts of it that are open to more than one reading.
20	
21	## 2. Tech stack and deployment
22	
23	- C# / ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10)
24	- PostgreSQL 18
25	- Entity Framework Core (Npgsql provider)
26	- Docker + Docker Compose
27	- JSON REST API under `/api/v1`
28	
29	The service runs with the existing `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` at the repository root: an `api` container (ASP.NET Core, port 8080) and a `db` container (PostgreSQL 18). The api container receives the database connection string as `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (configuration key `ConnectionStrings:HubDb`). In the CI pipeline, tests that need the database receive a connection string in the `RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB` environment variable.
30	
31	The service also provides `GET /api/v1/health`, which returns 200 when the database is reachable and 503 when it is not.
32	
33	## 3. Repository layout
34	
35	- Application code: project `ResourceHub.Api` in `PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/`
36	- Tests: project `ResourceHub.Tests` in `PA2/functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/`
37	- Build and run files (`ResourceHub.slnx`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props`) stay at the repository root and expect these project names and paths. `Directory.Build.props` turns on NuGet lock files (`packages.lock.json`), which the Dockerfile and pipeline restore in locked mode
38	
39	## 4. Roles
40	
41	| Role | What they do in this service |
42	|---|---|
43	| Course instructor | Submits resource request tickets for their course |
44	| Research lab faculty advisor | Submits resource request tickets for their research lab |
45	| IT director | Signs off on tickets (approves or rejects) |
46	| Administrator | Manages the asset catalog and runs the allocation that issues keys, vouchers and hardware |
47	
48	## 5. Standardized specification (verbatim)
49	
50	### Domain #2 The Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub:
51	
52	This service handles the distribution of critical project assets, logging tracking parameters, software license keys, and cloud credit vouchers across active course groups and research labs.
53	
54	**Functional Requirements:**
55	
56	1. Asset Lifecycle & Inventory Allocation: Programmatically manage and monitor a pool of physical lab equipment (hardware units, laptops, IoT nodes), software license keys, and cloud credit vouchers. Each unique asset must be assigned a UUID, name, category, total stock, and availability metrics. Assets are allocated directly to an overarching academic course or research lab.
57	2. Polymorphic Balance and Status Tracking: Process transactional balance logic for heterogeneous assets. For cloud vouchers, it must manage strict numeric deduction checks (preventing balances from dropping below zero) and log high-value alphanumeric license tokens. For physical items, it must calculate active check-out duration tracking rules and maintain status flags (available, reserved, checkedout, overdue).
58	3. Help Desk Ticketing Pipeline: Process incoming resource requests from course instructor or research lab faculty advisor. The service must parse multi-tiered requests, track ticket lifecycles (pending, approved, rejected, allocated, closed), update project asset allocations dynamically upon IT director sign-off, and output comprehensive logging metrics.
59	4. Explicit Inventory Allocation Engine: The system must decouple administrative ticket review from physical inventory modification. Inventory values must only alter when a separate, dedicated allocation execution command is processed by an administrator, triggering atomic database deductions and issuing keys or hardware assignment tokens.
60	5. Complex Multi-Field Query: Support rich administrative and group queries. Users can search and filter the asset catalog and ticket logs simultaneously by status, asset category, requesting research lab or course.
61	
62	**REST APIs**
63	
64	| Endpoints | Verbs | Description |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `/api/v1/assets` | POST, GET | Add an inventory asset item. Supplying multi-field search query parameters allows administrators and teams to filter active inventory listings by department program or availability state. |
67	| `/api/v1/assets/{asset_id}` | GET, PUT, DELETE | Read, update, and delete an inventory asset item. |
68	| `/api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/return` | POST | Processes the return of a checked-out physical device, increments the pool's remaining capacity stock, and records the return timestamp. |
69	| `/api/v1/assets/allocations` | GET | Read all active resource allocations, checked-out inventory metrics, and assigned software keys for a specific requesting research lab or course. |
70	| `/api/v1/assets/tickets` | POST, GET | Submit a new help desk resource request ticket or read a listing of all active requests filtered dynamically by status (pending/approved/allocated) or course section or project. |
71	| `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | PUT, DELETE, GET | Update a ticket's contents, delete a pending request, or fetch specific ticket metrics. A PUT request targeting this route handles the operational approval state transition. |
72	| `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}/allocate` | POST | Executes the real physical database mutation. This endpoint processes an approved ticket, atomically subtracts items from the main asset pool inventory, and establishes the active user allocation record. |
73	
74	## 6. Clarifications
75	
76	Where section 5 is open to more than one reading, build to these.
77	
78	1. **Kinds of asset:** each asset has a **type** (`physical`, `license`, `voucher`), which decides how its balance and status work, and a **category** (for example laptop, IoT node, IDE license, cloud credits), which is a descriptive label used for searching.
79	2. **Asset data:** UUID, name, type, category, home department program, total stock and availability. By type: a physical asset has a number of units and a default loan period in days; a license asset holds its license keys; a voucher asset holds a credit balance.
80	3. **Availability:** physical: number of units available, plus counts by status flag. License: keys not yet issued. Voucher: remaining balance. The availability filter on `GET /api/v1/assets` uses the status flags in requirement 2; license and voucher assets count as available while some stock or balance remains.
81	4. **When stock changes:** total stock is set when an asset is added or updated. Remaining stock and balances change only when a ticket is allocated (`POST .../allocate`) or a physical device is returned (`POST .../return`). The below-zero check in requirement 2 is made at allocation.
82	5. **License keys:** keys are stored with their asset, and each issued key is recorded with the ticket it was issued for and the time it was issued.
83	6. **Check-out duration:** a physical device's due date is its allocation date plus the loan period. A ticket may give a loan period for each physical asset it requests; otherwise the asset's default applies. A device is overdue once its due date has passed and it has not been returned.
84	7. **Ticket content:** a requester (a course instructor or a research lab faculty advisor), the course or the research lab the request is for, an optional project id, and one or more requested assets, each with a quantity (physical and license assets) or an amount (voucher assets). "Multi-tiered" means one ticket can request several assets.
85	8. **Ticket changes:** a ticket's contents can be updated, and the ticket deleted, only while it is `pending`. A PUT on `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` also changes its state: `pending` to `approved` or `rejected` (IT director sign-off), and `allocated` to `closed`. Only `POST .../allocate` moves a ticket from `approved` to `allocated`.
86	9. **Not enough stock:** allocation is all or nothing. If any requested asset does not have enough stock or balance, nothing is allocated and the ticket stays `approved`, so allocation can be run again later.
87	10. **What allocation issues:** license: keys from the asset's pool. Voucher: the requested amount, deducted from the balance. Physical: one hardware assignment token for each device handed out, with its due date.
88	11. **Return:** one device per call, identified by its hardware assignment token. The return adds one to the asset's remaining stock and records the return time.
89	12. **Active allocations:** physical devices not yet returned, and license and voucher allocations whose ticket is not `closed`.
90	13. **Logging metrics:** an event is recorded for every ticket state change and every allocation attempt, including attempts that fail for lack of stock. `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` returns the ticket with its events and timings (for example time from submission to approval and from approval to allocation).
91	14. **Filters:** query parameters can be combined. Assets: category, department program, availability. Tickets: status, asset category, course, research lab, project. Listings are paged and sorted newest first by creation date by default.
92	15. **Mock data:** courses (each including its section), research labs, projects, users and a few starting assets are seeded as static mock data with fixed ids, listed below, so tests and manual calls can use them. Each user has one of the four roles named in section 4: course instructor, research lab faculty advisor, IT director, administrator. No other service is called.

| `/api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/return` | POST | Processes the return of a checked-out physical device, increments the pool's remaining capacity stock, and records the return timestamp. |
| `/api/v1/assets/allocations` | GET | Read all active resource allocations, checked-out inventory metrics, and assigned software keys for a specific requesting research lab or course. |
| `/api/v1/assets/tickets` | POST, GET | Submit a new help desk resource request ticket or read a listing of all active requests filtered dynamically by status (pending/approved/allocated) or course section or project. |
| `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | PUT, DELETE, GET | Update a ticket's contents, delete a pending request, or fetch specific ticket metrics. A PUT request targeting this route handles the operational approval state transition. |
| `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}/allocate` | POST | Executes the real physical database mutation. This endpoint processes an approved ticket, atomically subtracts items from the main asset pool inventory, and establishes the active user allocation record. |

## 6. Clarifications

Where section 5 is open to more than one reading, build to these.

1. **Kinds of asset:** each asset has a **type** (`physical`, `license`, `voucher`), which decides how its balance and status work, and a **category** (for example laptop, IoT node, IDE license, cloud credits), which is a descriptive label used for searching.
2. **Asset data:** UUID, name, type, category, home department program, total stock and availability. By type: a physical asset has a number of units and a default loan period in days; a license asset holds its license keys; a voucher asset holds a credit balance.
3. **Availability:** physical: number of units available, plus counts by status flag. License: keys not yet issued. Voucher: remaining balance. The availability filter on `GET /api/v1/assets` uses the status flags in requirement 2; license and voucher assets count as available while some stock or balance remains.
4. **When stock changes:** total stock is set when an asset is added or updated. Remaining stock and balances change only when a ticket is allocated (`POST .../allocate`) or a physical device is returned (`POST .../return`). The below-zero check in requirement 2 is made at allocation.
5. **License keys:** keys are stored with their asset, and each issued key is recorded with the ticket it was issued for and the time it was issued.
6. **Check-out duration:** a physical device's due date is its allocation date plus the loan period. A ticket may give a loan period for each physical asset it requests; otherwise the asset's default applies. A device is overdue once its due date has passed and it has not been returned.
7. **Ticket content:** a requester (a course instructor or a research lab faculty advisor), the course or the research lab the request is for, an optional project id, and one or more requested assets, each with a quantity (physical and license assets) or an amount (voucher assets). "Multi-tiered" means one ticket can request several assets.
8. **Ticket changes:** a ticket's contents can be updated, and the ticket deleted, only while it is `pending`. A PUT on `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` also changes its state: `pending` to `approved` or `rejected` (IT director sign-off), and `allocated` to `closed`. Only `POST .../allocate` moves a ticket from `approved` to `allocated`.
9. **Not enough stock:** allocation is all or nothing. If any requested asset does not have enough stock or balance, nothing is allocated and the ticket stays `approved`, so allocation can be run again later.
10. **What allocation issues:** license: keys from the asset's pool. Voucher: the requested amount, deducted from the balance. Physical: one hardware assignment token for each device handed out, with its due date.
11. **Return:** one device per call, identified by its hardware assignment token. The return adds one to the asset's remaining stock and records the return time.
12. **Active allocations:** physical devices not yet returned, and license and voucher allocations whose ticket is not `closed`.
13. **Logging metrics:** an event is recorded for every ticket state change and every allocation attempt, including attempts that fail for lack of stock. `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` returns the ticket with its events and timings (for example time from submission to approval and from approval to allocation).
14. **Filters:** query parameters can be combined. Assets: category, department program, availability. Tickets: status, asset category, course, research lab, project. Listings are paged and sorted newest first by creation date by default.
15. **Mock data:** courses (each including its section), research labs, projects, users and a few starting assets are seeded as static mock data with fixed ids, listed below, so tests and manual calls can use them. Each user has one of the four roles named in section 4: course instructor, research lab faculty advisor, IT director, administrator. No other service is called.

Here's the plan. I've read the whole spec. This folder is empty, and .NET SDK 10.0.403 and Docker are installed.

## Data model (EF Core, PostgreSQL)

**Mock reference data** (seeded with the fixed ids from section 7):
- `Course` (id, code and section, title, department program)
- `ResearchLab` (id, name, department program)
- `Project` (id, name, course id or lab id)
- `User` (id, name, role, course id or lab id). Roles are `CourseInstructor`, `LabAdvisor`, `ItDirector` and `Administrator`.

**Assets**
- `Asset`: id, name, `Type` (physical, license or voucher), category, department program, total stock, remaining stock, created and updated times, and a concurrency token. The rest depends on the type:
  - physical: units and a default loan period in days
  - license: total and remaining count the keys
  - voucher: `TotalBalance` and `Balance` (numeric(12,2))
- `LicenseKey`: id, asset id, key value, issued ticket id, issued time. Keys are unique per asset.

**Tickets**
- `Ticket`: id, requester id, course id **or** lab id (exactly one), optional project id, status, and timestamps (created, approved or rejected, allocated, closed).
- `TicketItem`: ticket id, asset id, quantity (physical and license) **or** amount (voucher), and an optional loan period in days (physical only).
- `TicketEvent`: ticket id, event type, from and to status, actor id, detail, time. Event types are submitted, updated, approved, rejected, allocation_succeeded, allocation_failed and closed.

**Allocations**
- `Allocation`: ticket id, asset id, type, quantity or amount, allocation time. License keys link back to the ticket through `LicenseKey.IssuedTicketId`.
- `DeviceAssignment`: hardware token, allocation id, asset id, ticket id, checkout time, due time, return time.

**Physical status flags** are computed, not stored:
- **available:** the remaining units
- **reserved:** units requested on `approved` tickets that haven't been allocated yet
- **checkedout:** assignments not yet returned and not past their due date
- **overdue:** assignments not yet returned and past their due date

**Atomic allocation:** one transaction with conditional deductions (`UPDATE … SET remaining = remaining - n WHERE remaining >= n`). If any line fails, the whole transaction rolls back, a separate `allocation_failed` event is written and the API returns 409. The ticket stays `approved`.

## Choices I'd make

I'll log all of these in the notes.

- **Who is acting:** there is no authentication in scope, so the caller sends an `X-User-Id` header with a mock user's id, and the API checks that user's role. Unknown user → 401, wrong role → 403. The rules:
  - Asset POST, PUT and DELETE, allocate, and close: administrator
  - Approve or reject: IT director
  - Ticket create: course instructor or lab advisor, only for their own course or lab
  - GET routes: no header needed
- **Route clash:** I'll constrain `{asset_id:guid}` so that `/assets/tickets` and `/assets/allocations` don't match the asset route.
- **Database schema:** created with EF migrations, applied at startup and in the test fixture.
- **Paging:** `page` and `pageSize` parameters (default 20, maximum 100), returned with `items`, `total`, `page` and `pageSize`.
- **Errors:** RFC 7807 problem details.
- **Changing total stock** (PUT) is rejected if it would drop below the number already issued.
- **Deleting an asset** is rejected (409) if any ticket or allocation refers to it.

## Test approach

I'll use xUnit with `WebApplicationFactory` against real PostgreSQL. The connection string comes from `RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB`. Each test class gets its own fresh database, and if the variable isn't set, the database tests are skipped. Locally I'll run a Postgres 18 container to test against.

## Build order (each step: test → watch it fail → code → watch it pass)

1. Health: 200 when the database is reachable, 503 with a bad connection string.
2. Seeded mock assets can be read back by their fixed ids.
3. Asset CRUD: create, get, put and delete, plus validation (400), not found (404) and role checks (403).
4. Asset filters: category, department, availability and type, combined; paging and newest-first order.
5. Ticket submit: content validation (requester role, course xor lab, items valid for the asset type) and GET by id.
6. Ticket list filters: status, asset category, course, lab and project.
7. Ticket PUT: content edits only while pending; transitions pending→approved/rejected and allocated→closed (anything else is 409); DELETE only while pending.
8. Allocate:
   - license keys issued, voucher balance deducted, physical tokens with due dates
   - not approved → 409
   - not enough stock → nothing changes, ticket stays approved, failure event logged
   - two allocations run at the same time can't overdraw stock
9. Return: by token, stock goes up by one, return time recorded, a second return → 409; the overdue flag works.
10. Active allocations: GET by course or lab, excluding returned devices and closed tickets.
11. Ticket metrics: events and timings (submission→approval, approval→allocation).

## Files I'll create (all under this folder)

- `src/ResourceHub.Api/`:
  - `ResourceHub.Api.csproj`, `Program.cs`, `appsettings.json`
  - `Data/` (`HubDbContext`, `SeedData`, `Migrations/`)
  - `Domain/` (entities and enums)
  - `Contracts/` (request and response DTOs)
  - `Endpoints/` (`HealthEndpoints`, `AssetEndpoints`, `TicketEndpoints`, `AllocationEndpoints`)
  - `Services/` (`AllocationService`, `ActorResolver`)
- `tests/ResourceHub.Tests/`:
  - `ResourceHub.Tests.csproj`
  - `Infrastructure/` (`HubApiFactory`, `DbFact` skip attribute)
  - one test file per area above
- `packages.lock.json` for both projects, since the root `Directory.Build.props` requires lock files.
- Notes file `../../../MyAI/PA2/2026-11-14_01_resource-hub-build.md`.

To check that the project names, paths, target framework and test command line up, I'll need to read these root files at the start of the build. # ---- build stage: .NET SDK ----
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Restore first so the package layer is cached between code changes.
COPY global.json Directory.Build.props ./
COPY PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/packages.lock.json src/ResourceHub.Api/
RUN dotnet restore src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj --locked-mode

COPY PA2/functional-codebase/src/ src/
RUN dotnet publish src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj \
    --configuration Release --no-restore --output /app/publish /p:UseAppHost=false

# ---- runtime stage: ASP.NET Core runtime ----
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080
EXPOSE 8080

COPY --from=build /app/publish .

# Built-in non-root user in the .NET images.
USER $APP_UID

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "ResourceHub.Api.dll"]

# AI Contribution Weight: [100%] AI Generated / [0%] Human Refactored
# DevSecOps pipeline: build + test, Docker image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud.
#
# Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run.
# Scanner steps use continue-on-error and never set a failing exit code, so
# findings are reported (logs + artifacts) without blocking.

name: DevSecOps

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: "true"
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: "true"
  # Scanner images pinned by version and digest.
  TRIVY_IMAGE: aquasec/trivy:0.75.0@sha256:af6acf9a6b85dfe389a1941505c0ce9efef52a4719635e1a962f022a3d855daa
  SEMGREP_IMAGE: semgrep/semgrep:1.180.0@sha256:529ee8a277ec8adc5b534d7c74eea0a47e9de21d62852b6ba7ac6ba9566845c3
  API_IMAGE: resourcehub-api:ci

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      # Lets the health endpoint's "database reachable" test run in CI.
      postgres:
        image: postgres:18
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: resourcehub
          POSTGRES_USER: resourcehub
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ci_only_password
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U resourcehub -d resourcehub"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10

    env:
      SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
      RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB: Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=ci_only_password

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Shallow clones should be disabled for a better relevancy of analysis

      - name: Set up .NET (version from global.json)
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0
        with:
          global-json-file: global.json

      - name: Set up JDK 21 (SonarQube scanner)
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          java-version: 21
          distribution: zulu

      - name: Cache SonarQube Cloud packages
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.sonar/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar
          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar

      - name: Cache SonarQube Cloud scanner
        id: cache-sonar-scanner
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/scanner
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar-scanner
          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar-scanner

      - name: Install SonarQube Cloud scanner
        if: steps.cache-sonar-scanner.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner"
          dotnet tool update dotnet-sonarscanner --tool-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner"

      - name: Restore (locked to packages.lock.json)
        run: dotnet restore ResourceHub.slnx --locked-mode

      # ---- SonarQube Cloud wraps the one and only build ----
      # Skipped when SONAR_TOKEN is unavailable (e.g. pull requests from forks).
      - name: SonarQube begin
        if: env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner/dotnet-sonarscanner" begin \
            /k:"essieanawalt_cs763-resource-hub" \
            /o:"essieanawalt" \
            /d:sonar.token="$SONAR_TOKEN" \
            /d:sonar.host.url="https://sonarcloud.io" \
            /d:sonar.exclusions="evidence/**,PA1/**" \
            /d:sonar.cs.opencover.reportsPaths="PA2/functional-codebase/tests/**/TestResults/**/coverage.opencover.xml" \
            /d:sonar.cs.vstest.reportsPaths="PA2/functional-codebase/tests/**/TestResults/*.trx"

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build ResourceHub.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore

      - name: Test
        run: >-
          dotnet test ResourceHub.slnx --configuration Release --no-build
          --logger trx
          --collect "XPlat Code Coverage;Format=opencover"

      - name: SonarQube end (upload analysis)
        if: always() && env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner/dotnet-sonarscanner" end /d:sonar.token="$SONAR_TOKEN"

      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: PA2/functional-codebase/tests/**/TestResults/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload SonarQube report task
        if: always() && env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: sonarqube-report
          # Holds the dashboard URL and task id; the full report lives on sonarcloud.io.
          path: .sonarqube/out/.sonar/report-task.txt
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # ---- Docker image ----
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: docker build --tag "$API_IMAGE" .

      # ---- Trivy: dependencies (packages.lock.json) and image ----
      - name: Trivy dependency scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE":/src:ro \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" fs /src \
              --scanners vuln \
              --skip-dirs '**/bin' --skip-dirs '**/obj' --skip-dirs 'reports' --skip-dirs '.sonarqube' --skip-dirs 'evidence' --skip-dirs 'PA1' \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-deps.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --scanners vuln --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-deps.$ext" /out/trivy-deps.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-deps.txt

      - name: Trivy image scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" image "$API_IMAGE" \
              --scanners vuln \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-image.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --scanners vuln --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-image.$ext" /out/trivy-image.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-image.txt

      - name: Upload Trivy reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: trivy-reports
          path: reports/trivy/
          if-no-files-found: warn

  semgrep:
    name: Semgrep (C# static analysis)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Open-source CLI with public registry rules: no Semgrep account or token.
      - name: Semgrep scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/semgrep
          docker run --rm \
            -e SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off \
            -e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/src \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE":/src \
            -w /src \
            "$SEMGREP_IMAGE" semgrep scan \
              --config p/csharp \
              --exclude 'evidence' \
              --exclude 'PA1' \
              --metrics=off \
              --sarif-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.sarif \
              --json-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.json \
              --text-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.txt

      - name: Upload Semgrep reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: semgrep-reports
          path: reports/semgrep/
          if-no-files-found: warn

# Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub

ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) + PostgreSQL 18. See [spec-domain2.md](spec-domain2.md) for the full design.

**Current state: barebones.** Only `GET /api/v1/health` exists. It checks the PostgreSQL
connection through an EF Core `DbContext` (no tables yet).

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/     # Web API (Controllers/, Data/, Program.cs)
PA2/functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/ # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
```

## Prerequisites

- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
- Docker with Compose v2

## Run with Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

Expected when the database is up:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
```

Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
```

Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.

The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.

## Build and run locally (without the api container)

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
dotnet run --project PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api
```

Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
`PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).

## Test

```bash
dotnet test
```

Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
container and point the tests at it:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |

## NuGet lock files

Each project has a `packages.lock.json` that pins every direct and transitive package. CI and the
Dockerfile restore with `--locked-mode`, so a restore that would change the lock file fails. After
adding or upgrading a package, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files. Trivy also
reads these files to find NuGet dependencies; without them it detects none.

## CI (GitHub Actions)

`.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests.

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube | Restore, SonarQube begin, build (Release), test (with a PostgreSQL 18 service container, coverage), SonarQube end, `docker build`, Trivy dependency scan, Trivy image scan |
| Semgrep | Open-source Semgrep CLI with the public `p/csharp` rules (no account or token) |

Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run. Scanner findings
are reported in the logs and uploaded as artifacts (`trivy-reports`, `semgrep-reports`,
`sonarqube-report`, `test-results`) without failing the run. SonarQube Cloud results are on
the SonarQube Cloud dashboard; it needs the `SONAR_TOKEN` repository secret and is skipped
when the secret is not available (for example, pull requests from forks).

Manages lab equipment, software license keys and cloud credit vouchers, and the help desk
tickets that request them: submit → IT director sign-off → administrator allocation → return
(physical devices) → close. All endpoints in spec section 5 are implemented, following the
clarifications in section 6, with the section 7 mock data seeded under its fixed ids.

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
PA2/functional-codebase/dotnet-tools.json        # local dotnet-ef tool (migrations)
PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/     # Web API
  Program.cs                 #   services, JSON options, startup migration, routes
  Domain/                    #   entities and enums
  Data/                      #   HubDbContext, SeedData (spec section 7), Migrations/
  Contracts/                 #   request/response records
  Endpoints/                 #   Health, Asset, Ticket, Allocation route groups
  Services/                  #   AllocationService, validation, caller identity, views
PA2/functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/ # xUnit API integration tests (WebApplicationFactory + PostgreSQL)
```

## API

All routes are under `/api/v1`. Bodies and responses are JSON; enum values are lower snake case
(`physical`, `license`, `voucher`; `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `allocated`, `closed`).
Errors are RFC 7807 problem details (`400` validation, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409` state or stock conflicts).

| Route | Verb | Who (`X-User-Id`) | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/health` | GET | anyone | `200` if the database is reachable, `503` if not |
| `/assets` | POST | administrator | Add an asset. Physical: `units`, `defaultLoanDays`. License: `licenseKeys`. Voucher: `balance` |
| `/assets` | GET | anyone | Filters (combinable): `category`, `departmentProgram`, `availability` (`available`/`reserved`/`checkedout`/`overdue`), `type`, `search`; `page`, `pageSize` (≤100); newest first |
| `/assets/{asset_id}` | GET, PUT, DELETE | GET anyone; PUT/DELETE administrator | PUT sets total stock (cannot drop below what is handed out). DELETE refused (`409`) once tickets refer to the asset |
| `/assets/{asset_id}/return` | POST | administrator | Body `{"token": "HW-…"}`: returns one device, stock +1, records the return time |
| `/assets/allocations` | GET | the course's instructor / lab's advisor, IT director, administrator | `courseId` or `researchLabId`: unreturned devices, keys and credits on tickets not closed, plus a summary |
| `/assets/tickets` | POST | course instructor (own course) or lab advisor (own lab) | `courseId` or `researchLabId`, optional `projectId`, `notes`, `items: [{assetId, quantity \| amount, loanDays?}]` |
| `/assets/tickets` | GET | anyone | Filters: `status` (comma-separated), `assetCategory`, `courseId`, `researchLabId`, `projectId`; paged, newest first |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | GET | anyone | Ticket with `events` and `metrics` (seconds between steps, allocation attempts) |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | PUT | requester (content, while pending); IT director (`{"status":"approved"\|"rejected","reason":…}`); administrator (`{"status":"closed"}`) | Content edit **or** state change, not both |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | DELETE | requester or administrator | Pending tickets only |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}/allocate` | POST | administrator | Atomic, all-or-nothing: issues keys, deducts credits, hands out devices with tokens and due dates. Short stock → `409` with `shortages`, ticket stays `approved` |

**Caller identity.** Authentication is out of scope, so callers send a seeded user's id in the
`X-User-Id` header (unknown or missing → `401`, wrong role → `403`):

| User | Role | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Dr. Maya Chen | Course instructor, CS501 A1 | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` |
| Prof. Daniel Okafor | Course instructor, EE580 B1 | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002` |
| Dr. Lucas Ferreira | Lab advisor, Data Science Lab | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003` |
| Dr. Priya Raman | Lab advisor, Embedded Systems Lab | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004` |
| Jordan Blake | IT director | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005` |
| Sam Rivera | Administrator | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006` |

Course, lab, project and asset ids are in spec section 7.

# Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub

ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) + PostgreSQL 18. See [spec-domain2.md](spec-domain2.md) for the full design.

**Current state: barebones.** Only `GET /api/v1/health` exists. It checks the PostgreSQL
connection through an EF Core `DbContext` (no tables yet).

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/     # Web API (Controllers/, Data/, Program.cs)
PA2/functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/ # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
```

## Prerequisites

- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
- Docker with Compose v2

## Run with Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

Expected when the database is up:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
```

Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
```

Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.

The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.

## Build and run locally (without the api container)

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
dotnet run --project PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api
```

Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
`PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).

## Test

```bash
dotnet test
```

Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
container and point the tests at it:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |

## NuGet lock files

Each project has a `packages.lock.json` that pins every direct and transitive package. CI and the
Dockerfile restore with `--locked-mode`, so a restore that would change the lock file fails. After
adding or upgrading a package, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files. Trivy also
reads these files to find NuGet dependencies; without them it detects none.

## CI (GitHub Actions)

`.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests.

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube | Restore, SonarQube begin, build (Release), test (with a PostgreSQL 18 service container, coverage), SonarQube end, `docker build`, Trivy dependency scan, Trivy image scan |
| Semgrep | Open-source Semgrep CLI with the public `p/csharp` rules (no account or token) |

Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run. Scanner findings
are reported in the logs and uploaded as artifacts (`trivy-reports`, `semgrep-reports`,
`sonarqube-report`, `test-results`) without failing the run. SonarQube Cloud results are on
the SonarQube Cloud dashboard; it needs the `SONAR_TOKEN` repository secret and is skipped
when the secret is not available (for example, pull requests from forks).

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"healthy","database":"reachable"}
```

On start-up the api applies the EF Core migrations, which create the tables and seed the
mock data. If the database is down at that moment the api keeps running and reports `503`;
restart the api container once the database is back.

### Example flow

```bash
B=http://localhost:8080/api/v1
```

Dr. Chen asks for two laptops (10-day loan), one IDE key and 250 credits for CS501 A1:

```bash
curl -s -X POST $B/assets/tickets -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" -d '{"courseId":"10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","projectId":"30000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","items":[{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","quantity":2,"loanDays":10},{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","quantity":1},{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","amount":250.00}]}'
```

The IT director approves it (use the ticket `id` from the response):

```bash
curl -s -X PUT $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id> -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005" -d '{"status":"approved"}'
```

The administrator allocates it. The response holds the issued key and the device tokens:

```bash
curl -s -X POST $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id>/allocate -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006"
```

Return one laptop, then close the ticket:

```bash
curl -s -X POST $B/assets/50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002/return -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006" -d '{"token":"<HW-token>"}'
```

```bash
curl -s -X PUT $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id> -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006" -d '{"status":"closed"}'
```

`GET $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id>` shows the events and timings.

input.new_string:
Manages lab equipment, software license keys and cloud credit vouchers, and the help desk
tickets that request them: submit → IT director sign-off → administrator allocation → return
(physical devices) → close. All endpoints in spec section 5 are implemented, following the
clarifications in section 6, with the section 7 mock data seeded under its fixed ids.

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
PA2/functional-codebase/dotnet-tools.json        # local dotnet-ef tool (migrations)
PA2/functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/     # Web API
  Program.cs                 #   services, JSON options, startup migration, routes
  Domain/                    #   entities and enums
  Data/                      #   HubDbContext, SeedData (spec section 7), Migrations/
  Contracts/                 #   request/response records
  Endpoints/                 #   Health, Asset, Ticket, Allocation route groups
  Services/                  #   AllocationService, validation, caller identity, views
PA2/functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/ # xUnit API integration tests (WebApplicationFactory + PostgreSQL)
```

## API

All routes are under `/api/v1`. Bodies and responses are JSON; enum values are lower snake case
(`physical`, `license`, `voucher`; `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `allocated`, `closed`).
Errors are RFC 7807 problem details (`400` validation, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409` state or stock conflicts).

| Route | Verb | Who (`X-User-Id`) | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/health` | GET | anyone | `200` if the database is reachable, `503` if not |
| `/assets` | POST | administrator | Add an asset. Physical: `units`, `defaultLoanDays`. License: `licenseKeys`. Voucher: `balance` |
| `/assets` | GET | anyone | Filters (combinable): `category`, `departmentProgram`, `availability` (`available`/`reserved`/`checkedout`/`overdue`), `type`, `search`; `page`, `pageSize` (≤100); newest first |
| `/assets/{asset_id}` | GET, PUT, DELETE | GET anyone; PUT/DELETE administrator | PUT sets total stock (cannot drop below what is handed out). DELETE refused (`409`) once tickets refer to the asset |
| `/assets/{asset_id}/return` | POST | administrator | Body `{"token": "HW-…"}`: returns one device, stock +1, records the return time |
| `/assets/allocations` | GET | the course's instructor / lab's advisor, IT director, administrator | `courseId` or `researchLabId`: unreturned devices, keys and credits on tickets not closed, plus a summary |
| `/assets/tickets` | POST | course instructor (own course) or lab advisor (own lab) | `courseId` or `researchLabId`, optional `projectId`, `notes`, `items: [{assetId, quantity \| amount, loanDays?}]` |
| `/assets/tickets` | GET | anyone | Filters: `status` (comma-separated), `assetCategory`, `courseId`, `researchLabId`, `projectId`; paged, newest first |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | GET | anyone | Ticket with `events` and `metrics` (seconds between steps, allocation attempts) |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | PUT | requester (content, while pending); IT director (`{"status":"approved"\|"rejected","reason":…}`); administrator (`{"status":"closed"}`) | Content edit **or** state change, not both |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | DELETE | requester or administrator | Pending tickets only |
| `/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}/allocate` | POST | administrator | Atomic, all-or-nothing: issues keys, deducts credits, hands out devices with tokens and due dates. Short stock → `409` with `shortages`, ticket stays `approved` |

**Caller identity.** Authentication is out of scope, so callers send a seeded user's id in the
`X-User-Id` header (unknown or missing → `401`, wrong role → `403`):

| User | Role | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Dr. Maya Chen | Course instructor, CS501 A1 | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` |
| Prof. Daniel Okafor | Course instructor, EE580 B1 | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002` |
| Dr. Lucas Ferreira | Lab advisor, Data Science Lab | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003` |
| Dr. Priya Raman | Lab advisor, Embedded Systems Lab | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004` |
| Jordan Blake | IT director | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005` |
| Sam Rivera | Administrator | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006` |

Course, lab, project and asset ids are in spec section 7.

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"healthy","database":"reachable"}
```

On start-up the api applies the EF Core migrations, which create the tables and seed the
mock data. If the database is down at that moment the api keeps running and reports `503`;
restart the api container once the database is back.

### Example flow

```bash
B=http://localhost:8080/api/v1
```

Dr. Chen asks for two laptops (10-day loan), one IDE key and 250 credits for CS501 A1:

```bash
curl -s -X POST $B/assets/tickets -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" -d '{"courseId":"10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","projectId":"30000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","items":[{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","quantity":2,"loanDays":10},{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","quantity":1},{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","amount":250.00}]}'
```

The IT director approves it (use the ticket `id` from the response):

```bash
curl -s -X PUT $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id> -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005" -d '{"status":"approved"}'
```

The administrator allocates it. The response holds the issued key and the device tokens:

```bash
curl -s -X POST $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id>/allocate -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006"
```

Return one laptop, then close the ticket:

```bash
curl -s -X POST $B/assets/50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002/return -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006" -d '{"token":"<HW-token>"}'
```

```bash
curl -s -X PUT $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id> -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006" -d '{"status":"closed"}'
```

`GET $B/assets/tickets/<ticket-id>` shows the events and timings.
